About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

As Stripe’s user base and global footprint grows dramatically, we have distinctly unique support problems resulting from both our type of scale and the type of businesses we partner with. The Stripe Delivery Center (SDC) strategy will provide operational leverage and expand Stripe’s portfolio of operational capabilities to support the scaled needs for external users and internal Stripe teams.

Stripe is launching Stripe Delivery Centers - a new global team to design, implement and grow Stripe’s operations for the next decade. We are looking for dynamic and curious people that have a passion for solving global user issues, building operations, driving process improvements and that want to play a front-line role in building this new operational capability for Stripe and accelerating Stripe’s growth.
In this role, you will recruit, manage, and develop a group of Operations Associates that are focused on user support. This person will cultivate the happiness of their team members while guiding them to be the best they can be, through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and advocacy within the organization.

This means helping to set team goals, and using metrics to efficiently measure and guide team performance in pursuit of those goals. To be a fit, you will have a strong operations mindset, be able to move quickly, and be passionate about delivering an incredible user experience.

Recruit, manage, coach, and develop a new team of in-office Operations Associates
Drive strong operational delivery and process improvement helping to mitigate risk while balancing operational efficiency and user impact
Identify gaps in current systems, policies and strategies, and recommend enhancements and process improvements to mitigate risks
Build a great culture and ensure team members are happy, effective, and growing in their career
Set clear goals and direction, and provide regular feedback on team members’ performance
Be data-driven in your analysis of performance, and in your decision making
Transmit and foster our values, serving as a beacon of Stripe’s user-centric philosophy and culture of transparency, empathy, inclusion, and empowerment

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

At least 8+ years experience leading operations support teams
Experience working cross-functionally with multiple teams to deliver high impact initiatives

Excellent written and verbal communication skills
An ability to partner effectively with internal stakeholders
Background of identifying and remediating quality gaps in team performance
Passion for process improvement and innovation
Ability to periodically work a weekend day for which you will receive a weekday off; the SDC operates during daytime hours with shifts from the morning through early evening

Experience in building and scaling new teams from zero
Strong operational background including experience with new process launches and service delivery in a high growth technology company

Join us in building the future of finance.
Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers.

We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Tax Operations team’s mission is to support our tax information reporting and compliance efforts related to the purchase and sale of equities and crypto.

We collaborate closely with internal partners to ensure robust processes and data flows. We are dedicated to ensuring a high standard of compliance in a fast-paced and collaborative team environment.
Robinhood is looking for a skilled Tax Operations Analyst to join our team! We are seeking driven individuals who thrive in a fast-paced environment and can manage multiple priorities. In this role, you will work on executing various exception reports covering areas such as reporting, withholding, and cost basis. You will also help our Customer Experience and Account Operations teams handle tax-related inquiries and resolve reporting issues.
This role is based in our New York, NY and Menlo Park, CA offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

Collaborate with our product, project, and engineering teams to launch, improve and scale Robinhood products and systems
Contribute to and track various tax related projects such as new product launches and promotions
Help our Customer Experience and Account Ops teams handle tax related inquiries and resolve reporting and withholding issues, including areas such as withholding, cost basis, retirement accounts, and crypto tax reporting
Develop and assist with the implementation of reconciliations of data between internal systems and vendors, as well as verification of data being sent from the tax reporting vendor to IRS
Work on executing various exception reports covering areas such as reporting, withholding and cost basis, while implementing internal policies and procedures
Work on building and maintaining dashboards for metrics and checklists to manage and change workflows and queries to improve team functions as well as to improve customer experience
Work with various Robinhood entities and departments to streamline data flow as well as automate processes where possible

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or similar field
3-5+ years of work experience in tax, accounting, and/or operations
High attention to detail
Ability to manage and drive projects to completion in a deadline driven environment
Strong analytical and communication skills

The GTM Strategy & Operations Analyst will join a global team driving Datadog’s next phase of growth. We are interdisciplinary thinkers with diverse backgrounds across investment banking, management consulting, investment management, strategy, and operations. Our team partners directly with Datadog’s senior leaders to set growth strategy, improve business efficiency, support data-driven decision-making, and run complex operations across the company.

In this role, you will be embedded within Sales as a dedicated operational partner to field managers and Account Executives. You will help manage account flow across sellers, support day-to-day field operations, and stay close to the sales floor to understand the challenges sellers face.

You will use those insights to build processes, analyses, and lightweight tools that help the field move faster and operate more effectively. A key focus of this role will be identifying opportunities to incorporate AI into core workflows to improve both the speed and quality of operational support.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

· Own core account management processes for a Sales segment, including account distribution, account movement, account prioritization, and coverage optimization across teams and AEs.

· Serve as a subject matter expert on account management operations, advising sales leaders on territory structure, account flow, and opportunities to improve seller coverage.

· Support field decision-making through business reporting and analysis, including quarterly business reviews, performance metrics, root cause analysis, pipeline health, and coverage gap identification.

· Act as the dedicated operational point of contact for regional AEs and frontline managers, handling ad hoc operational requests and supporting Salesforce hygiene, including opportunity updates, field accuracy, and pipeline cleanliness.

· Resolve Rules of Engagement conflicts as an impartial advisor to the field, balancing speed, fairness, and alignment to Datadog’s core sales processes.

· Experiment with and embed AI into field support workflows, including prototyping lightweight automations, AI-assisted analyses, and ecosystem integrations that help AEs and managers take faster, better-informed action.

· Develop a deep understanding of seller workflows and operational pain points, then design process improvements and build business cases for enhancements based on field-observed inefficiencies.

· Partner with Revenue Operations and Global Strategy & Operations to ensure process changes, tooling updates, and data governance decisions are implemented cleanly and adopted by the field.

· Bachelor’s degree.

· 1-3 years of experience in GTM, Revenue, Sales Operations, Strategy & Operations, or a related analytical role, ideally within a SaaS or high-growth B2B technology company.

· Strong analytical skills, with experience using Excel or Google Sheets to organize data, conduct analysis, and generate insights.

· Effective written and verbal communicator who can clearly explain operational issues, recommendations, and next steps to cross-functional partners.

· Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple requests, track follow-through, and maintain accuracy in fast-moving environments.

· Self-starter with a strong work ethic, high ownership, and the ability to operate independently with guidance.

· Curious learner who enjoys picking up new tools, systems, and business processes.

· Collaborative problem-solver who enjoys working closely with others to improve how teams operate.

· Experience working directly with frontline sales teams in a field-facing operations role.

· Prior experience with GTM functions, revenue operations, sales strategy, or growth strategy initiatives.

· Experience using Salesforce or other CRM systems.

· Familiarity with AI/LLM tools, prompt engineering, workflow automation, or lightweight tool prototyping.

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Sr. Operations Manager to oversee the operations of our fulfillment center in Philipsburg, New Jersey. As the Sr. Operations Manager, you will be responsible for managing a team of 300+ associates and ensuring efficient and effective functioning of the facility.

Your exceptional leadership, strategic thinking, and operational expertise will be crucial in driving the success of our fulfillment center.

This role will require expertise in managing both direct-to-consumer (D2C) and business-to-business (B2B) fulfillment operations, with a hands-on approach to driving efficiency, cost reduction, and customer satisfaction. Join us to build and develop a world-class fulfillment center and contribute to the continued growth of Flexport.

Provide strong leadership, guidance, and mentorship to the entire team, fostering a positive and productive work environment.
Manage and develop a high-performing team of 300+ associates, including hiring, training, coaching, and performance management.
Lead a team of 10 salaried employees, including department managers and supervisors, ensuring their success and alignment with organizational goals

Oversee the day-to-day operations of the fulfillment center, ensuring efficient and accurate processing of orders, inventory management, and shipping for both D2C and B2B customers.
Develop and implement operational strategies to optimize productivity, quality, and customer satisfaction.
Establish operational distinctions for D2C vs. B2B fulfillment, ensuring proper flow paths, picking methodologies, and shipping requirements are met.
Continuously monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics to drive continuous improvement and achieve operational targets.
Foster a culture of safety, ensuring compliance with all applicable health and safety regulations and implementing measures to minimize workplace accidents and injuries.

Develop and manage the fulfillment center's budget, ensuring financial objectives are met while maintaining operational excellence.
Identify opportunities to optimize costs, reduce waste, and improve overall operational efficiency without compromising quality or service levels.
Implement cost control measures and monitor expenses, ensuring adherence to budgetary guidelines.

Collaborate with other departments such as logistics, procurement, customer service, and quality control to ensure seamless coordination and integration of processes.
Partner with the Regional General Manager to align fulfillment center strategies with overall company goals and objectives.
Provide regular reports, updates, and insights to senior management on operational performance, challenges, and opportunities.

Drive a culture of continuous improvement, fostering innovation, and identifying opportunities for process optimization, automation, and technology advancements.
Stay abreast of industry trends, best practices, and emerging technologies related to fulfillment center operations, and implement relevant changes as appropriate.

Bachelor's degree in business administration, logistics, supply chain management, or a related field (advanced degree preferred).
Proven experience as a Site Leader or similar leadership role, preferably in a large-scale fulfillment center or distribution environment.
Strong knowledge of fulfillment center operations, including order processing, inventory management, warehousing, and shipping.
Demonstrated success in managing and developing large teams of both hourly and salaried employees.
Exceptional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate teams to achieve goals.
Proficiency in analyzing data, metrics, and KPIs to drive performance improvements.
Solid financial acumen and experience in budgeting, cost management, and driving operational efficiency.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment while maintaining attention to detail and ensuring accuracy.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with a strategic mindset.
Familiarity with warehouse management systems (WMS) and other relevant software applications.
Knowledge of health and safety regulations and best practices in a warehousing environment.
If you are a dynamic and results-oriented professional with a proven track record in managing large fulfillment centers, we invite you to apply for this challenging and rewarding position. Join our team and contribute to the success of our mission.

Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.

At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.

As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.

Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

As a Senior Health Data Analyst, you will focus on analyzing health data within the Veeva Compass product suite. Veeva Compass delivers record-level prescription and medical claims data to power longitudinal, de-identified patient analytics for commercial use cases—including patient journey, market landscape, and provider engagement.

You will be responsible for driving data quality, consistency, and standardization within the Terminology Reference Library (TRL) by managing reference data for key attributes found across prescription and medical claims—including drug information, ICD-10 diagnosis codes, procedure and lab codes, as well as payer and plan data.

In this role, you will query prescription and medical claims datasets to support the evaluation and integration of new inbound data sources into core schemas.

Additionally, you will define and track key quality metrics via interactive dashboards, contributing to technical documentation and validation reports to ensure our reference data remains accurate, scalable, and seamlessly integrated across all Veeva products.

Drive TRL Governance: Maintain and expand the Terminology Reference Library (TRL), managing core reference datasets across prescription and medical claims (including drug information, ICD-10 codes, procedure/lab codes, and payer/plan data).
Evaluate & Integrate New Data: Conduct deep-dive data querying, field mapping, and structural analysis on potential new data sources to evaluate fit and integrate them into existing core schemas.
Execute Quality & Cleansing Workflows: Perform exploratory data analysis to identify discrepancies, handle missing values, execute deduplication, and ensure data completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.
Continuous Product Improvement: Investigate data anomalies within the Veeva Compass product suite, testing both planned and unplanned data changes to assess downstream customer impact.
Build Metrics & Documentation: Develop interactive dashboards to track key data quality metrics, contributing to technical documentation, validation reports, and team process improvements.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Data Scientists, Product Managers, and Developers to articulate data quality nuances, uncover root causes, and build robust data pipelines.

4+ years of experience analyzing record-level prescription and medical claims datasets.
4+ years of experience in health data quality analysis, data profiling, and data governance principles.
Advanced SQL proficiency, with extensive experience querying, manipulating, and aggregating large-scale relational databases.
Deep working knowledge of healthcare code sets and industry standards, including NDC, ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS, LOINC, and payer/plan reference data.
Proven track record in data storytelling: Experience analyzing, visualizing, and demonstrating data quality findings to stakeholders using Excel, BI tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Sigma), or interactive dashboards.
Strong problem-solving mindset: Eagerness to dive deep into complex, unstructured healthcare data issues, identify root causes, and propose innovative solutions.
Bachelor’s degree in a STEM, quantitative, or healthcare informatics field, or equivalent practical experience

Experience in Python
Experience with the BI tool Sigma
Experience in life science industry

About Ramp
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

As a member of Ramp’s AML Team, you will play a key role in executing Ramp’s anti–money laundering and sanctions compliance program. You will be responsible for conducting investigations, filing SARs, driving process improvement, and supporting AI and automation initiatives for the AML program.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced fintech environment, has strong analytical and investigative skills, and is excited about building scalable processes to support Ramp’s growth. You’ll work closely with our Compliance, Risk, Product, and Fraud Operations teams to ensure Ramp maintains a strong financial crimes compliance program.

Review and disposition escalations from transaction monitoring alerts and internal referrals, conducting full investigations and determining reporting obligations
Draft and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and Unusual Activity Reports (UARs), ensuring narratives are accurate, defensible, and submitted within required timeframes
Flex into Sanctions, PEP, and KYC/EDD workflows as needed
Perform secondary peer reviews
Assist in the ongoing optimization of Ramp’s AML systems and tooling, including rule tuning, automation implementation, and testing
Drive workflow design updates, process improvements and simplification, and contribute to maintenance of procedures and training materials
Support responses to bank partner requests, audits, and regulatory reporting and obligations
Triage and respond to escalations from internal teams to Compliance
What You Need
Minimum 4 years of experience in compliance advisory or operations teams, with at least 2 years as an AML investigator in an operations team (1LOD or 2LOD)
Experience drafting and filing SARs/UARs
Demonstrated familiarity with Sanctions, EDD, KYC/KYB and financial crimes compliance
Ability to handle multiple and fast-changing priorities
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
Strong Investigative and critical thinking skills

AI fluency, with experience delivering automation/AI solutions in compliance
Accreditation by ACAMS, an equivalent industry body, or other qualifications in the areas of financial crime, risk management, or compliance
Experience supporting a growing compliance team
Experience in high-growth start-ups, particularly in Fintech
Experience working cross-functionally with key stakeholders such as risk, engineering, and operations teams

Design, launch, and continuously improve the process to engage overlay sales teams across new product lines, including clear entry criteria, required context, routing rules, and escalation paths

Surface operational risks, repeated failure modes, and process breakdowns early, then drive practical fixes that improve execution without creating unnecessary overhead

This is a hands-on operations role focused on running and sharpening the day to day operation. You will own the day-to-day execution of reconciliation and loss detection, resolve the issues that surface across both, and, just as importantly, make the work better every quarter by improving the process and automating the manual parts.

You won't just run the machine; you'll use AI and data tooling to reshape how the machine runs. Over time you'll build an end-to-end understanding of how money flows through the Gusto product, from a transaction all the way to the financials.
If you want a seat where operational excellence, a builder's instinct for process, and genuine curiosity about how money moves all matter, this is it.

Payments are at the core of Gusto's business, and the Platform Operations team is the foundation of financial trust behind them. We safeguard customer funds and keep financial operations accurate, transparent, and scalable, sitting as the connective tissue between Engineering and Accounting/Finance.

That means reconciling money movement, detecting and investigating losses, resolving exceptions as they come up, and continuously improving the processes and tooling that let us do all of it at scale.

Own reconciliation execution and exceptions research across customer cash and money movement, validating the accuracy of Gusto's financial data with internal and external partners.
Monitor transactions to detect discrepancies, anomalies, and potential losses; investigate promptly and drive issues to resolution.
Identify, escalate, track, and close individual payment related issues across reconciliation and loss domains, pulling in the right cross functional partners (Engineering, Accounting, Payments) to get each one resolved.
Contribute to the accuracy and timeliness of financial close and reporting for the areas you own.
Tighten the controls on the processes you own, whether manual or automated, and recommend enhancements that reduce risk and manual effort.
Partner with Engineering to trace recurring breaks and losses to their source and resolve the underlying product or system gaps, rather than absorbing them downstream.
Strengthen documentation so processes are durable, repeatable, and not person dependent.
Use AI to automate manual, repetitive workflows, chaining multiple steps to move from raw data to finished output and measurably reduce the time your work takes.
Share what you build so teammates can replicate it, raising the whole team's efficiency, not just your own.
Spot the most manual, repetitive, and high volume work in your domain and prioritize it for automation, going after the biggest reductions in effort first.

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related analytical field.
3-4 years in an operations, analyst, or similar role with a track record of high-quality, detail-heavy execution and strong ownership.
Experience in payments, banking, fintech, or financial services / accounting operations.
Familiarity with reconciliation, cash management, ACH/NACHA rules, or card networks.
Exposure to regulatory or compliance requirements (e.g., MTL) relevant to a payments environment.
Demonstrated use of AI to automate real, manual workflows, with specific examples of what you built, what it replaced, and the impact. You reach for AI to go from raw data to finished output, not just to draft an email.
Strong analytical and data skills: proficient in spreadsheets, and either working in SQL today or a clear aptitude and eagerness to learn it quickly.
Genuine curiosity about how money and financial systems connect. You want to understand the financial impact of your work and how the product behaves end to end.
A process improvement instinct: you get uncomfortable running the same manual process twice and instinctively look for the fix.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to own outcomes with minimal oversight, know when to escalate, and work cross functionally with technical and finance partners alike.
Comfort operating independently in a fast paced, ambiguous environment, confident standing up or reshaping a process rather than waiting for one to exist.

As our Senior Marketing Operations Manager (f/m/d) with a MarTech and attribution focus, you build and own plancraft's marketing measurement and technology layer. This is a hands-on build role. You design and implement the tracking, attribution, and analytics yourself.

You build the infrastructure that shows which channels and campaigns actually drive pipeline and revenue, across our markets. You make the numbers trustworthy and the stack scale. You work close to the Data team on clean, governed data, and close to Marketing on what the numbers need to answer.

Build multi-touch attribution end to end: select the model, set it up, and write the logic that connects spend to pipeline and revenue across channels. You build it, not just specify it.
Build and maintain the tracking layer yourself: tag management (GTM and server-side), the data layer, conversion pixels, and event taxonomy across web and ad platforms (Google, Meta, LinkedIn).
Set up GA4 and build the marketing analytics stack. Write the SQL reports and datasets from HubSpot, GA4, and the warehouse with the Data team.
Build marketing dashboards across channels, campaigns, and funnel stages, with metrics defined before launch: CAC, ROAS, conversion, and pipeline contribution by Bowtie stage.
Build and own the technical consent and GDPR layer: consent management platform, cookie governance, and server-side tracking that holds up legally.
Run the MarTech stack: tool selection, integrations, and data flow between HubSpot, ad platforms, GA4, and n8n. Keep one source of truth and remove parallel logic.
Scale tracking and data models into new markets (NL/ES/IT/PL) by design, not as one-off setups per country.
Build marketing automation (n8n) or apply AI tooling where it speeds up measurement and analytics work. This comes up occasionally and is not the core of the role; campaign automation sits with the Junior Marketing Operations Manager.
Partner with the Junior Marketing Operations Manager where execution meets measurement, and with the Data team on data governance.

Must-Have Skills
4+ years in marketing technology, web analytics, or marketing data and attribution.
Strong SQL for analysis and reporting.
Hands-on with tag management and tracking infrastructure: GTM and server-side GTM, data layer, conversion pixels, and GA4.
Built multi-touch attribution hands-on in a real funnel, not just managed a vendor who did.
Experience with visualization tools (Looker, Tableau, Power BI, or similar).
Technical grasp of GDPR, consent management, and cookie and tracking governance.
Background in B2B SaaS or a comparable data-driven environment.
Hands-on with HubSpot as both a marketing platform and a data source.
Nice-to-Have Skills
Python for advanced analytics or automation scripting.
Experience with CDPs or first-party data setups at scale.
Server-side tracking and cookieless measurement.
Comfortable with automation tooling (n8n or similar) and applying AI in marketing analytics.

The Technology Operations Manager provides leadership and oversight for operational technology services, with responsibility for driving long-term platform strategy while ensuring the effective execution of daily operations.

This role supports a technology ecosystem that includes AWS-based platforms, distributed data center environments, enterprise applications, and SaaS operational systems. This role takes a forward-looking approach to modern cloud-based architecture and operations, ensuring technology initiatives support broader business goals and customer success.

The organization’s platforms and services operate within a global, always-on environment, requiring exceptional standards for system performance, cybersecurity, availability, scalability, and operational resilience backed by continuous 24/7 support.

Primary responsibilities include overseeing the stability and performance of cloud and on-premises environments, leading application support and operational response processes, directing service delivery and technical operations teams, enabling scalable infrastructure for engineering initiatives, managing enterprise network and database services, and partnering closely with stakeholders across technology and business functions to support organizational objectives.

As a technology leader within the organization, you will drive visibility into operational KPIs in partnership with product and engineering teams, proactively mitigate risks to application performance and availability, and identify opportunities to improve reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency across platforms and services.

What You Will Do
Lead the evaluation, adoption, and execution of technology initiatives that enhance platform reliability, operational performance, and employee effectiveness across the organization. Recruit, mentor, and motivate a high-performance operations staff.
Oversee the administration of compute services including cloud, SD-WAN, virtual compute, storage, backups, disaster recovery, and local area networks.
Drive operational excellence through structured incident, problem, and change management practices, including ownership of root cause analysis and continuous service improvement initiatives.
Develop, manage, and report on database and operational SLAs.
Identify and mitigate potential risks that could negatively impact system reliability and availability.
What You Will Need
Minimum of 5 years leading and supporting globally distributed hybrid cloud infrastructure, including cloud transformation initiatives and modernization of legacy systems and applications.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering or comparable operational roles, with deep expertise in incident investigation, observability practices, service reliability, and root cause management.
Expert understanding of and previous hands-on experience with data center, virtualization, IaC, infrastructure, back office, and application engineering technologies.
Strong interpersonal, verbal, written, and technical skills to lead the day-to-day activities of the team and build strong relationships with the extended organization.
Ability to manage multiple projects to completion.
Ability to meet deadlines and work efficiently within a fast-paced environment.

Menschen mit unserem Web-Content.
Und wir sind noch lange nicht fertig.

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

You'll manage how target accounts get identified and prioritised, how signals get activated, how AI agents make decisions on each account, and how all of it feeds back into pipeline.
You're hands-on. You translate strategy into running plumbing across Marketing and SDR Operations, with ABM at the centre.
What you do
Design and build the workflows that turn DeepL's GTM motion into running systems. You work operationally across the Marketing, SDR and Sales org, anywhere a workflow can sharpen targeting, surface intent, or accelerate the activation of a target account.
Build automated GTM workflows: outbound, inbound, routing, enrichment, follow-up
Create target account lists and the workflows that keep our TAL current, qualified, and routed
Set up account research and enrichment workflows that surface context for reps and AI agents
Build AI agent workflows for account research, personalisation, and decisioning
Activate buying signals (intent, behaviour, product usage) into the right next action per account
Build account-based journeys across email, web, paid, SDR, and AE motions.
Define how a lead or account moves from signal to pipeline to revenue
Keep our CRM, analytics, and GTM tooling in shape: clean data, working integrations, real-time visibility
Build the reporting that links account engagement to pipeline progression

The Library (PL) is a major national art research center serving the National Gallery's staff, fellows and professors at the Center for Advanced Study in the Visual Arts, visiting art historians, the scholarly community at large and members of the public.

The library contains a wide-ranging collection of more than 525,000 books and periodicals on the history, theory and criticism of art and architecture, millions of images and a broad range of electronic resources.

Duties for this position include: Coordinates and monitors Library-wide administrative operations: Coordinates and monitors administrative and operational processes that cut across the library's departments.

Maintains visibility into the status of key actions, deadlines and requirements related to travel, records, timekeeping, personnel-related documentation and other cross-department administrative workflows.

Reviews the status of ongoing actions, identifies delays, inconsistencies or incomplete documentation and follows up with supervisors, staff and other Gallery offices to keep processes moving accurately and on time.

Coordinates budget, procurement, contracts, and related financial operations: Coordinates Library-wide budget, procurement, contracts, and related financial processes involving federal, trust and grant funds. Tracks expenditures, commitments, purchase card activity, requisitions and supporting documentation.

Maintains and updates operational trackers, reports and related tools that support budget monitoring, purchasing and planning. Reviews transactions and documentation for completeness, correct coding, timeliness and alignment with established requirements. Identifies issues that require correction, clarification or further review.

Coordinates with procurement, budget, accounting, travel, contracting and related offices to support timely processing of Library business. Researches and develops practical approaches, models, and tools to support budget formulation, multi-year budget planning, and operational decision-making.

Analyzes workflows and recommends operational improvements: Reviews administrative workflows and recurring business processes to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, clarity, compliance and coordination across departments.

Develops and maintains shared procedures, checklists, templates, timelines and tracking tools that improve continuity and reduce confusion or duplication. Uses judgment in applying established guidance to specific situations.

Resolves routine process issues independently and recommends practical improvements or corrective actions when problems recur or existing procedures are not working effectively. Leads or coordinates Library wide operational planning efforts, including space planning, to assess near-term needs. Develops preliminary recommendations for implementation.

Coordinates personnel-related processes, workforce support activities, records management and operational planning: Coordinates and tracks administrative processes and documentation related to personnel actions, onboarding, awards, performance-related processes, training, professional development and other workforce support activities.

Helps identify recurring operational issues that affect staff effectiveness. Reviews and improves the onboarding process for new staff, using existing onboarding documentation as a starting point and doing further research to strengthen it.

Coordinates records management activities for administrative records, including file structures, retention practices and disposition processes. Works with Archives and Library staff to identify paper and electronic records that fall under the records schedule and helps sort and organize them appropriately.

Designs and carries out processes for digitizing administrative files. Creates and maintains tracking systems and documents procedures to improve consistency, access, and records control. Gathers, organizes and maintains information needed for internal reporting, operational planning and management decision-making.

Serves as a key operational point of contact: Serves as a regular point of contact for Library staff and for colleagues in administrative offices across the Gallery on matters related to Library operations and administrative processes.

Explains established procedures and requirements related to procurement, travel, records, timekeeping, budget tracking and related operational matters. Communicates clearly, professionally and with discretion, especially when handling sensitive or confidential information.

We are hiring a Client Operations Coordinator to support the day-to-day social operations of a major US entertainment client.

Chase inputs, surface risks early, escalate blockers appropriately, and keep work moving across multiple teams and stakeholders

Strong organisation across multiple workstreams, deadlines, approval paths, versions, and dependencies
High ownership and a proactive approach to keeping work moving
Clear written communication and the ability to turn scattered feedback or ambiguous requests into concise actions, owners, and decisions

Approvals move through the correct stakeholders with accurate statuses, complete feedback, and no lost decisions

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic is expanding its reseller program in Japan and Korea.

As our Reseller Operations Manager for Japan and Korea, you'll own how resellers in both countries get onboarded, transact, get paid, and get supported, across both of our resale motions: hyperscaler resale, where partners resell Claude through the cloud marketplaces (AWS Bedrock today, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry to follow), and direct resale, where partners resell on Anthropic paper through our own quote-to-order and billing systems.

The global team builds the program; you make it work for Japanese and Korean partners and feed back what has to change.
This is an operator role, not a partner manager role. In the first months you'll be validating deal registrations and answering partner tickets yourself; by the end of the first year the volume should be running on documented process, service levels, and vendor or system coverage that you set up.

Own reseller onboarding for Japan and Korea end to end: application intake, screening coordination, agreement execution, marketplace authorization, entitlement setup, and activation, and keep the partner record in Salesforce decision-grade for both regions.
Run hyperscaler (3P) reseller operations: deal-registration intake and validation within SLA, marketplace authorizations and private-offer processing with the cloud alliance teams, and end-customer reporting on every reseller transaction so partner-sourced revenue can be attributed.
Run direct (1P) reseller operations: partner quotes and order forms, order booking and provisioning, and commit tracking and true-ups with Deal Desk, RevOps, and Accounting, and work with Finance and Tax on local invoicing, currency, and consumption-tax handling for each transaction route.
Run the regional side of reseller incentives: eligibility, validation of quarterly payouts, and partner disputes, in partnership with the global incentive operations team and Finance.
Stand up first-line operational support for resellers in Japanese and Korean during local business hours, inside the global partner support queue rather than alongside it, and localize the onboarding, deal-registration, and ordering content partners depend on.
Manage any outsourced or contracted operations capacity used in region (scope, quality, service levels) and coordinate with Enablement on the logistics of local-language certification and training.
Own reseller reporting for Japan and Korea: registration volume and cycle time, activation, attach, and attributed revenue by partner and by motion, and use it to tell the regional teams and the global program what to fix next.
Adopt the global Partner Operations playbooks where they fit, write the in-region variants where they don't, and represent Japan and Korea requirements in partner systems and automation work so manual volume doesn't grow with partner count.

Several years in channel, reseller, distribution, or partner operations at a technology company, ideally touching both a cloud-marketplace motion and a direct or contract-based resale motion.
Working proficiency in Japanese, Korean, and English. You'll run operational relationships with partners in both countries and work daily with a US-based team; proficiency doesn't need to be identical across all three, but you need to be able to work with partners in both regions.
Practical knowledge of how at least one major cloud marketplace's reseller program works (authorizations, private offers, deal registration), or deep experience in one motion and a track record of picking up the other quickly.
Hands-on experience with quote-to-order, order management, or partner billing, and the Finance, Deal Desk, and Legal coordination that comes with it.
A track record of taking a manual process and turning it into documented workflow, service levels, and reporting, including managing vendors or contractors who execute part of it.
Hands-on Salesforce experience (reporting, data maintenance), and comfort being the only operations person in the region while working with a team many time zones away.

Experience inside the Japanese or Korean enterprise reseller and systems-integrator ecosystem, including local invoicing, credit, and consumption-tax conventions.
Experience with partner incentive or rebate operations, or with a partner program during its launch phase.
Experience with PRM or deal-registration tooling, or building automations with Claude or similar tools to run operational workflows at volume.

s.h: How this role works with the team
s.t:
You'll report into Partner Experience and work day to day with two groups.

The global Partner Operations team in San Francisco owns the reseller program's systems, and playbooks; our reseller operations owner there is your direct counterpart, and you'll split work along a simple line: they own the global process, you own its execution and adaptation in Japan and Korea.

The Japan and Korea go-to-market teams own the partner relationships and the commercial conversations; you're the operational layer underneath them, and the person they come to when something about a partner's onboarding, order, or payout needs to move.

You'll also be the regional voice into Finance, Deal Desk, RevOps, and the cloud alliance teams on anything that has to work differently in these markets.

This role is focused on Jeeves ’s growth programs and emerging revenue channels — including our partnerships channel and new market expansion initiatives — where we need rigorous, scalable analytics to match the pace of growth.
You’ll be responsible for the analytical layer that connects our sales activity to revenue outcomes: building the dashboards our leadership relies on, maintaining shared responsibility for the integrity of our performance data, and proactively surfacing the insights that shape how we operate. You’ll work closely with the Head of Revenue Operations and contribute meaningfully to planning and review cycles alongside GTM leadership.
The pace here is real. Priorities shift, timelines compress, and the ground moves under your feet — not occasionally, but constantly. We need someone who is energized by that, not worn down. You won’t wait for someone to tell you what to look at. You’ll already know.

GTM Analytics & Growth Program Insights
Build and maintain Tableau dashboards tracking performance across our partnerships channel and new growth initiatives — serving audiences from country leads to executive leadership.
Analyze conversion rates, pipeline health, ramp trends, and revenue attainment across programs and segments, surfacing patterns before they become decisions that have already been made.
Come with a point of view. When a program is underperforming or a trend shifts, bring an interpretation and a recommendation (not just a chart).
Support quarterly and annual GTM business reviews with structured analysis: cohort breakdowns, market-level benchmarks, and forward-looking indicators.
Revenue Planning & Target Analysis
Contribute to GTM capacity planning and quota-setting cycles — modeling scenarios, building attainment reports, and stress-testing assumptions before plans are finalized.
Maintain performance-against-target reporting for growth programs and emerging channels: track attainment, flag outliers early, and ensure data is always reconciled.
Support variable compensation analysis for relevant programs — running calculations, auditing for accuracy, and partnering with Finance to ensure payouts are correct and timely.
Build and maintain data structures that support reliable rolling forecasts for new and high-growth segments.
AI-Driven Operations & Scale
Use AI tools, including Claude and other frontier models, as active parts of your workflow: automating repetitive reporting tasks, accelerating data synthesis, and building scalable analytical programs that would otherwise require a much larger team.
Identify RevOps processes that can be operationalized or significantly improved through AI, and take ownership of building those solutions, not just flagging the opportunity.
Apply AI-assisted analysis to extract insights at scale from large, multi-source datasets: pipeline signals, rep activity, customer behavior, and market trends.
Help establish Jeeves ’s AI-first approach to RevOps as a model for how the broader GTM team operates.
Data Quality & Systems Integration
Share responsibility for data quality across our revenue stack (HubSpot CRM, Tableau, and financial systems), conducting audits for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
Connect disparate data sources (CRM, marketing automation, financial tools, and proprietary revenue data) so that reporting on growth programs is unified and trustworthy.
Document data models, metric definitions, and reporting logic so the team works from a shared understanding of what we’re measuring and why.
Stakeholder Partnership
Develop enough context on our GTM motion to contribute meaningfully in planning and pipeline review cycles alongside sales leadership, bringing data that drives decisions, not just awareness.
Serve as a reliable analytical resource to the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM leadership: scope requests clearly, pull the data, and return clear answers quickly.
Identify process gaps and proactively propose improvements to how we collect, manage, and act on GTM data (especially across new and growing channels).

Technical & Analytical Skills
Tableau mastery: able to write complex calculated fields, build multi-source dashboards, and design views for diverse audiences from reps to the C-suite.
Advanced Excel and Google Sheets: complex formulas, pivot tables, and financial modeling — you reach for the right tool for the job, not just the most impressive one.
Strong SQL skills: you can get to an answer independently without waiting for a data engineer to pull it for you.
Data integration experience: comfortable connecting CRM, marketing automation, and financial data into unified reporting environments.
Business metrics fluency: deep understanding of conversion rates, customer lifetime value (LTV), pipeline coverage, ramp curves, revenue attainment, and customer health.
Data modeling: able to design clean structures that support accurate forecasting, compensation analysis, and multi-region rollups.
AI Fluency (Required, Not Optional)
You actively use AI tools, Claude Copilot/Code, or equivalent, as part of your day-to-day workflow, not as a novelty.
You’ve used AI to automate reporting pipelines, accelerate analysis, or build operational programs that scale beyond what a single analyst could do manually.
You’re curious about where AI can go next in RevOps and you bring ideas, not just execution.
Soft Skills & Ways of Working
Hungry and driven: you want to build something generational, and you bring the energy and output to match. You hold yourself to a higher standard than anyone else will hold you to.
Thrives in high-velocity environments: you’re not just comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — you’re energized by them. You find a way through, not a reason to wait.
High agency: you don’t wait for a ticket. You’re already thinking about what the data might be missing or what question leadership will ask next week.

Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners .
We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.
Since launching publicly in September 2023 , Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue , with a clear path to profitability by late 2026 . We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue) —the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
· Mission-critical problems : We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.
· High bar, low ego : Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.
· Speed over comfort : We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.
· Enduring impact : What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.
Team & Locations
We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.
Flex Fuels Ambition.

Flex is building its lifecycle marketing function from the ground up. We're looking for someone who can own both the strategy and the technical infrastructure behind how we engage prospects and customers across the credit application journey, banking, AP automation, and our broader product suite.
This is a builder's role: you'll be the first dedicated owner of lifecycle marketing at Flex, working directly with RevOps, Engineering, and Data to design the systems, not just the campaigns, that will power retention, activation, and growth as we scale.

You'll partner closely with the Director of Revenue Operations and Head of Revenue to shape lifecycle strategy, while also being hands-on in Braze, Segment, and our data infrastructure — there's no team to hand this off to yet, so you're doing the thinking and the building.
Flex doesn't have a dedicated product marketing team today, so this role also owns messaging — not just the systems that deliver it. You'll need to be comfortable using AI tools to accelerate copy drafting, and working directly with Product, Legal, and Compliance to shape and approve messaging for a regulated fintech audience, rather than relying on a product marketing team to hand you finished copy.
Because lifecycle touches so much of the customer journey, this role also needs to partner closely with Product to establish clear lines of ownership — what communications live in-product versus in lifecycle channels, and why.

Own lifecycle marketing strategy end-to-end: acquisition follow-up, application drop-off recovery, onboarding, activation, retention, and win-back across Flex's product suite (credit card, banking, AP automation, expense management, working capital)
Draft and own lifecycle messaging and copy directly (using AI tools to accelerate drafting), then partner with Product, Legal, and Compliance to shape and approve it for a regulated fintech audience — there's no product marketing team to hand this off to
Partner with Product to define and maintain clear ownership boundaries — which touchpoints are product-owned (in-app, transactional, native notifications) versus lifecycle-owned (email, SMS, re-engagement), and the rationale behind that split, so both teams can build without duplicating effort or working at cross-purposes
Partner directly with Engineering and Data to design event-based triggers and data architecture that power personalized, automated customer journeys — not just request the data, but help define what needs to be tracked and how
Build and own Braze infrastructure: Canvas flows, segmentation logic, dynamic content, and journey orchestration, working from a technical foundation you help define alongside RevOps and Data
Design and maintain the Segment-to-Braze data pipeline in partnership with Data/Engineering, ensuring clean identity resolution and reliable event tracking
Develop the measurement framework for lifecycle marketing: define the KPIs, build the reporting, and tie lifecycle performance to business outcomes like conversion, retention, and revenue
Bring judgment on prioritization and sequencing — deciding what infrastructure and campaigns to build first given Flex's current stage, rather than waiting to be told
Ensure lifecycle communications meet the compliance and disclosure standards required in a regulated fintech environment
Act as the internal expert on lifecycle marketing systems and strategy, briefing stakeholders (RevOps, Sales, CS, Leadership) on what's being built and why

6-8+ years of experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, or retention marketing, with meaningful time in fintech, financial services, or another regulated industry
Deep hands-on experience with Braze (or a comparable platform like Iterable/Customer.io) — you've built Canvases, not just launched campaigns someone else configured
Working fluency with Segment or similar CDPs, including identity resolution, event tracking, and data pipeline design
Proven experience partnering directly with Engineering and Data teams to design event-based systems, not just consuming what's handed to you
Strategic ownership experience: you've defined a lifecycle or retention strategy and the roadmap to execute it, not just run campaigns within someone else's framework
Strong analytical fluency — comfortable defining KPIs, building reporting frameworks, and using data to prioritize what to build next
Comfort with ambiguity and zero-to-one building; you don't need existing infrastructure or a team to make progress
Strong writing skills and comfort using AI tools to draft and iterate on messaging quickly, plus experience navigating legal/compliance review for customer-facing copy in a regulated industry — this role doesn't have a product marketing team to lean on
Bonus: B2B experience alongside B2C/D2C, and familiarity with BigQuery, dbt, or similar data warehouse tools
Why This Role Is Different

Master the Tasker lifecycle, using data-driven insights and strong data fluency to identify gaps, design and lead experiments, and communicate performance insights and business impact to teams and leadership.

About Motorway
Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships.

Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.
This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

We're now applying that same model to Enterprise: the part of the market where businesses, not private individuals, sell vehicles to dealers. It's 2 million of the 8 million used cars sold in the UK each year, a quarter of the total market.
In May 2026 we launched our Enterprise remarketing service with Mobilize Financial Services (the finance arm behind Renault, Nissan, Dacia and Alpine) as our first customer (see launch article here ).

Mobilize’s end-of-lease customers profile their car through Motorway’s market-leading app, we auction the vehicle directly to dealers, and the vehicle is collected from the customer at the end of the lease.

This cuts weeks out of a process that used to require physical storage sites and repeat transport, saving costs and time; and delivering a better customer experience.
This role joins the Enterprise team that is building this business line from the ground up. It's a rare chance to shape a new, fast-growing product inside an already fast-growing scale-up, and help rebuild a part of the automotive industry that our CEO has called "well overdue a rebuild." If you’re excited about building a ground-breaking business that redefines an industry, this role is for you.

You'll be joining an ambitious new chapter for Motorway from day one.

About Substrate
Substrate is the critical infrastructure layer between AI and biology. AI for biology has a data problem, not a compute problem: biological foundation models can predict but cannot experiment, and the large-scale, high-quality data they need does not exist. We are building the lab that generates it, with quality and provenance built in. We are not a CRO and we are not a cloud lab.
The company was founded by Mostafa ElSayed, co-founder and CEO; Oli Hoy, who leads the lab buildout and operations; Alexey Morgunov, who leads science and intelligence software; and Anna Huyghues-Despointes, who leads partnerships and go-to-market.

You will run the day-to-day operations of our lab in London, and be the person the scientists come to when something is missing, broken, late or lost. The day-one work is what you would expect: consumables and stock, goods in and cold chain, equipment servicing and calibration, suppliers and purchasing, waste streams and safety records.
Three parts go beyond a standard lab operations job. The first is provenance. Every experiment we sell carries a record of what went into it, down to the lot of the consumable used and the conditions material was held in. If a lot number is not captured, the data point is worth less, and that record runs through you.
The second is that the systems are not written yet. Inventory, goods in, asset registers and ordering exist in no form that will survive the next year. You define what the lab has to capture and work with the science and software teams to make sure it does.
The third is that sample handling and stock control here get automated, and you help specify the system that does it. Every sample, plate, reagent and consumable lot carries a barcode, scanned at each point it is handled, so the record is created by the work rather than reconstructed afterwards.

The same scan draws stock down, which turns reordering from a weekly count into something the system flags before anyone is short. Our software team is building that layer now and the requirements have to come from the lab floor: what gets a barcode, where the scan points sit, and what happens when a label will not read.

Some find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing which one you are.
Your first 90 days
First 30 days
Take ownership of goods in: every delivery received, booked in, stored correctly and recorded.
Map how material moves through the lab and build the first accurate picture of what we hold. That map is the input to a fully barcoded scheme and system.
Days 30 to 60
Put a working inventory and reorder system in place, with minimum levels set from real consumption rather than guesses, and own the purchasing loop.
Agree the barcode and labelling scheme with the software team, and get equipment records in one place.
Days 60 to 90
Run the lab as a routine that does not depend on being asked, with the barcoded system live across one workflow, goods-in to bench to stock draw-down, feeding our provenance record.

You have run the physical side of a lab where being out of stock stops the work: biotech, pharma, a university or institute lab, or a manufacturing or diagnostics operation built around one.

Lab consumables and the rhythm of a working lab are already familiar to you, you have handled real volume and real inventory, and you know the difference between a system that works on paper and one that works at eight on a Monday morning.

We are not asking for a particular speciality, but you should arrive able to run the lab rather than learn what one needs.

Two or more years running a lab or comparable physical operation, hands-on and accountable for the result.
Practical stock control: goods in, inventory records, reorder points, stock counts that reconcile.
Buying from suppliers: raising orders, comparing quotes, managing lead times.
Hands-on with a barcoded or scanned stock system, including what goes wrong when people skip the scan.
Lab environment experience: cold storage, hazardous waste, containment, controlled materials.

Health and safety training such as IOSH.
Developed or co-developed a barcode system for autonomous workflows in labs, including working with software development teams to implement it.
How we work and who you will work with
This role is on site five days a week at 20 Triton Street in London, because the lab is a physical place and the work is in it. The wider founding team is distributed across London, New York and Europe.

You will report to Simon Varzandeh, a member of our scientific staff working on protein characterisation and one of the lab's heaviest users, and work alongside the protein science and functional genomics teams, the engineers building the tracking and stock system with you, and operations on facilities, health and safety and purchasing.

You will be the first person here whose whole job is focused on the lab floor.
We work in the open and each person owns their area. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover.

About the Client
An SEC-registered investment advisor operating a tech-driven multi-manager hedge fund platform is hiring a Fund Operations Manager to take ownership of NAV production and reconciliation as its fund count scales.
The firm is an eight-person, fully distributed team onboarding approximately eight new custom funds in the near term. Fund operations currently sit with a single Head of Operations plus an onshore outsourced provider, and the firm is bringing that work in-house. The systems already work — what the team needs is capacity and sharper process as complexity grows.

Reporting to the Head of Operations, this role splits roughly 50% NAV and fund accounting, 25% management company financials, and 25% investor operations and ad hoc projects. The first 30 days are spent shadowing a full month-end close cycle, with delegated ownership of core workflows by day 60 and transition of outsourced reconciliation work by day 90. Success means owning specific fund operations workflows end-to-end with minimal oversight and answering Limited Partner questions independently.

About Gusto
At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

Payments at Gusto aren't just infrastructure — they're the reason people get paid on time, every time. Payment Operations sits within Gusto's Money team, a cross-functional group spanning Engineering, Product, and Operations that powers money movement across Gusto's growing product surface: core payroll, contractor payments, international money movement, and new business offerings like PEO.
As a Payment Operations Analyst, you'll own specific end-to-end payment workflows, resolve exceptions that require real judgment, and help make our systems more reliable and efficient over time. Gusto's payment surface area is expanding — and this team is at the center of that growth.
This is a role for someone who can shift from investigating a single misfired transaction to coordinating a response on a payment outage affecting thousands — and bring the same rigor to both. You think in systems. You hold partners accountable. You lead with curiosity and embrace AI as a core part of how you work.
You'll collaborate closely with Engineering, Product, Accounting, Risk, and CX — and you'll develop strong day-to-day relationships with Gusto's bank and payment partners. When something breaks or slows down, you're the one who drives it to resolution.

Support the payment lifecycle end-to-end
Own the operational layer of specific payment workflows — ACH processing, exception handling, refunds, collection re-debits, reconciliation. When something is off, you investigate, escalate where needed, and see it through to resolution. And when you see a pattern, you push to fix the root cause.
Build alongside Product and Engineering
Payment Operations doesn't just react — we shape how the systems work. You'll contribute to product specs, surface operational pain points, help define requirements, and participate in launches. You're a partner in building, not just a consumer of what gets shipped.
Close the loop on customer pain
Customer and CX feedback is signal. You actively mine it to identify friction in payment flows, prioritize what matters, and bring those insights into the operational and product conversations where decisions get made.
Think in systems
Connect the dots across rails, partners, reconciliation, compliance, and customer experience. When an issue surfaces, you understand how it ripples — and you bring that perspective to cross-functional conversations.
Hold partners to a high standard
Work directly with Gusto's bank and payment partners — domestic and international — to triage issues, resolve escalations, and maintain strong working relationships. You know how to be firm and collaborative at the same time, and you don't let things sit.
Lead with AI
You use AI as a genuine work partner — to move faster on analysis, draft communications, synthesize data, and automate the repetitive. You're always looking for the smarter way to get to the answer.

3+ years of experience in payment operations, banking operations, treasury operations, or a related role at a fintech or financial institution
Working knowledge of domestic payment rails (ACH/Nacha, wires, RTP) and/or international money movement (cross-border transfers, FX, global disbursement networks); experience across both is a strong plus
Strong analytical instincts — you look for the pattern behind the problem and can query or structure data to find it (SQL a plus but not required)
Experience working with bank portals, payment processors, or reconciliation tools
Ability to communicate clearly with both operational and technical counterparts; you can write a crisp Slack to an engineer and a professional escalation to a bank partner
Comfortable working in ambiguity and taking ownership without waiting for perfect information
Eager to build AI into how you work — whether you're already using it daily or just getting started, you see it as a genuine productivity lever and are committed to developing that fluency
Knowledge of relevant compliance frameworks (Nacha operating rules, unclaimed property, money transmission) is a strong plus

ADESA, a Carvana owned company, currently operating over 50 locations throughout the US. Our auto auctions, some up to 200 acres, provide a wide array of vehicle services including repair & reconditioning, auction remarketing, and many of our sites serve as market hub distribution centers. Our inventory comprises hundreds of thousands of vehicles across North America from retail to commercial, OEM & more.
We work in a service industry and embrace a “we” versus “I” culture – help others, and they will help you. Our industry is fun, fast-paced, and competitive – and filled with the best people who are passionate about what they do.
We’re excited about the future! As an industry leader, ADESA is poised for a multi-year expansion including huge investments in facilities, massive sales growth, and an ever-increasing inventory of vehicles! We are looking for great people who want to take this journey with us!
Role and Team
Reporting to the Regional Director, the General Manager is responsible for driving the Auction to success through effective leadership. This role is the primary leader for the site, setting the tone for customer and employee experience and executing strategies to support financial performance and company initiatives. The General Manager is expected to embody the company values and influence and lead others as a people, customer, and business manager for their location.

Identify opportunities for business growth. Regularly meet with customers, attend sales visits with Sales staff and other customer engagement opportunities. Make sure customers receive prompt, efficient and courteous attention for all contacts and transactions.
Act as change champion for the site. Understand, navigate, communicate, and ensure successful adaptation of change initiatives. Ensure proper follow-through on all directives, bulletins and schedules from the Corporate Office and Regional Director. Maintain a good flow of communication with Corporate Office, RD, key contacts within the company, and external contacts.
Attend a Profit and Loss Statement review each accounting period with the RD. Ensure accurate and timely reconciliation of accounting with weekly and monthly corporate reports. Initiate and follow up on discrepancies. Monitor accounts receivable and report variances to RD, Controller and Central Office. Control regular and overtime payroll and other business expenses to support business operations and financial objectives.
Monitor KPI’s and expectations. Leverage technology and tools available. As appropriate, develop and implement action plans to support improvements, and celebrate successes.
Be familiar with procedures for handling all aspects of customer disputes and resolve any customer complaints in a friendly, courteous manner. Escalate issues to RD as necessary.
Identify, hire, train, and mentor the management of today and the future for the auction. Support recruiting, hiring and onboarding initiatives to meet business needs and corporate/legal requirements. Promote, develop and train all employees according to company guidelines.
Maintain positive employee relations and morale. Practice sound leadership and human relations principles to promote teamwork at all times. Set a good personal example of attitude and performance. Follow-through and communicate employee relations problems to the Regional Vice President and Human Resource team as appropriate.

Evaluate and take positive, consistent, disciplinary action on infractions of company policies and procedures as defined in the employee disciplinary policy. Prepare and conduct performance appraisals for direct report employees and support the performance appraisal process for the team.
Conduct employee meetings at least once a month or as necessary to communicate Company and Department issues and build teamwork among the employees. Maintain a good flow of communication with Regional Vice President, and other pertinent personnel.
Account for and identify all auction inventory; monitor and report unusual activity and notify RD and appropriate corporate teams as necessary.
Monitor and control all site related conditions, vehicles, property and equipment within corporate standards for cleanliness, proper maintenance and safety. Advise Maintenance of all breakdowns and maintenance immediately. Ensure good routine preventive maintenance.
Make sure all Department area conditions do not threaten employee or customer safety. Respond to and follow proper procedures on employee and customer accidents, injuries, and loss or damage to any property. Report all incidents immediately. Ensure functional specifications are sound, efficient and support ADESA goals.

Practice and instruct all employees in proper loss prevention and reaction procedures. Account for and identify all keys, codes or other safety or security information. Report all incidents properly and immediately.

The Loan Operations Analyst will support the Fund Accounting and Controllership teams during monthly and quarterly closing, helping ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting.

Interest in developing expertise in institutional/alternative portfolio management and investment or insurance accounting solutions.

Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.

Self-starter with a proactive and results-driven approach.

Demonstrated initiative, curiosity, and adaptability in managing evolving business needs.
Positive, “can-do” attitude and a desire to contribute to a culture of continuous improvement and excellence.
